warnings: Some admissions factor ratings were not identified. Check C7 in the original PDF; blank or unrecognized ratings are not inferred.
Admissions policies may refer to a later application cycle than the reported cohort.

Source: exact archived VT-authored original from CollegeData.fyi; publisher now requests email inquiries for current and historical CDS files. The working archived file URL and SHA-256 identify the source actually reviewed.

Publisher inconsistency: 2024 overall applicants are 52,296 (CDS-C!C49), while in-state and out-of-state applicant answers sum to 52,498 (C60 + C65); international 4,921 is separately reported (C70). The source does not explain whether the out-of-state count includes international students. Headline counts preserve explicit overall answers; no residency total is inferred. The gender rows report zero unknown-gender applicants but 122 unknown-gender admits; those source answers are retained.

The 2024 file is a question/answer dictionary, not a visual CDS form. Blank answers are excluded from matching text outside C1, preventing printed score-band boundaries from becoming percentiles. Worksheet cells and original labels are retained.

Offline worksheet adapter: source page numbers identify CDS worksheets A=1 through J=10, not physical PDF pages. The browser importer supports PDF extraction and reviewed JSON imports; it does not extract XLSX files.
The contradictory unknown-gender applicant answer (0 versus 122 admitted) remains in original worksheet evidence; its normalized applicant metric is left unfilled.

review_status: C1 counts checked against original PDF pages or worksheet cells; additional metrics source-extracted

metrics.gpa_basis: Source-reported GPA; schools may use different weighting. Distribution percentages cover GPA reporters in the labeled group.

enrolled.method: sum of PDF gender/status counts; cross-checked with PDF residency table Total column; cross-checked with sum of PDF residency counts

applicants.method: visually reviewed explicit overall Total; source gender breakdown disagrees

I3. Undergraduate Class Size
In the table below, please use the following definitions to report information about the size of classes
and class sections offered in the Fall 2023 term.
✓ Please include classes that have been moved online in response to the COVID-19 pandemic.
Class Sections: A class section is an organized course offered for credit, identified by discipline and
number, meeting at a stated time or times in a classroom or similar setting, and not a subsection such as a
laboratory or discussion session. Undergraduate class sections are defined as any sections in which at least
one degree-seeking undergraduate student is enrolled for credit. Exclude distance learning classes and
noncredit classes and individual instruction such as dissertation or thesis research, music instruction, or
one-to-one readings. Exclude students in independent study, co-operative programs, internships, foreign
language taped tutor sessions, practicums, and all students in one-on-one classes. Each class section should
be counted only once and should not be duplicated because of course catalog cross-listings.
Class Subsections: A class subsection includes any subsection of a course, such as laboratory, recitation,
and discussion subsections that are supplementary in nature and are scheduled to meet separately from the
lecture portion of the course. Undergraduate subsections are defined as any subsections of courses in
which degree-seeking undergraduate students enrolled for credit. As above, exclude noncredit classes and
individual instruction such as dissertation or thesis research, music instruction, or one-to-one readings.
Each class subsection should be counted only once and should not be duplicated because of cross-listings.
Using the above definitions, please report for each of the following class-size intervals the number of class
sections and class subsections offered in Fall 2023. For example, a lecture class with 800 students who
met at another time in 40 separate labs with 20 students should be counted once in the “100+” column in
the class section column and 40 times under the “20-29” column of the class subsections table.

H - Financial Aid!A1=H. FINANCIAL AID
H - Financial Aid!B3=Please refer to the following financial aid definitions when completing Section H.
H - Financial Aid!B5=Awarded aid: The dollar amounts offered to financial aid applicants.
H - Financial Aid!B6=Financial aid applicant: Any applicant who submits any one of the institutionally required financial aid applications/forms, such as the FAFSA.
H - Financial Aid!B7=Indebtedness: Aggregate dollar amount borrowed through any loan program (federal, state, subsidized, unsubsidized, private, etc.; excluding parent loans) while the student was enrolled at an institution. Student loans co-signed by a parent are assumed to be the responsibility of the student and should be included.
H - Financial Aid!B8=Institutional scholarships and grants: Endowed scholarships, annual gifts and tuition funded grants for which the institution determines the recipient.
H - Financial Aid!B9=Financial need: As determined by your institution using the federal methodology and/or your institution's own standards.
H - Financial Aid!B10=Need-based aid: College-funded or college-administered award from institutional, state, federal, or other sources for which a student must have financial need to qualify. This includes both institutional and non-institutional student aid (grants, jobs, and loans).
H - Financial Aid!B11=Need-based scholarship or grant aid: Scholarships and grants from institutional, state, federal, or other sources for which a student must have financial need to qualify.
H - Financial Aid!B12=Need-based self-help aid: Loans and jobs from institutional, state, federal, or other sources for which a student must demonstrate financial need to qualify.
H - Financial Aid!B13=Non-need-based scholarship or grant aid: Scholarships and grants, gifts, or merit-based aid from institutional, state, federal, or other sources (including unrestricted funds or gifts and endowment income) awarded solely on the basis of academic achievement, merit, or any other non-need-based reason. When reporting questions H1 and H2, non-need-based aid that is used to meet need should be counted as need-based aid.
H - Financial Aid!B14=Note: Suggested order of precedence for counting non-need money as need-based:
H - Financial Aid!C15=1. Non-need institutional grants | H - Financial Aid!D15=6. Non-need outside grants
H - Financial Aid!C16=2. Non-need tuition waivers | H - Financial Aid!D16=7. Non-need student loans
H - Financial Aid!C17=3. Non-need athletic awards | H - Financial Aid!D17=8. Non-need parent loans
H - Financial Aid!C18=4. Non-need federal grants | H - Financial Aid!D18=9. Non-need work
H - Financial Aid!C19=5. Non-need state grants
H - Financial Aid!B20=Non-need-based self-help aid: Loans and jobs from institutional, state, or other sources for which a student need not demonstrate financial need to qualify.
H - Financial Aid!B21=Private student loans: A nonfederal loan made by a lender such as a bank, credit union or private lender used to pay for up to the annual cost of education, less any financial aid received.
H - Financial Aid!B22=External scholarships and grants: Scholarships and grants received from outside (private) sources that students bring with them (e.g., Kiwanis, National Merit scholarships). The institution may process paperwork to receive the dollars, but it has no role in determining the recipient or the dollar amount awarded.
H - Financial Aid!B23=Work study and employment: Federal and state work study aid, and any employment packaged by your institution in financial aid awards.

     In the table below, please use the following definitions to report information about the size of classes and class

    Class Sections: A class section is an organized course offered for credit, identified by discipline and number,
     meeting at a stated time or times in a classroom or similar setting, and not a subsection such as a laboratory or
     discussion session. Undergraduate class sections are defined as any sections in which at least one degree-seeking
     undergraduate student is enrolled for credit. Exclude distance learning classes and noncredit classes and individual
      instruction such as dissertation or thesis research, music instruction, or one-to-one readings. Exclude students in
     independent study, co-operative programs, internships, foreign language taped tutor sessions, practicums, and all
     students in one-on-one classes. Each class section should be counted only once and should not be duplicated
    because of course catalog cross-listings.


    Class Subsections: A class subsection includes any subsection of a course, such as laboratory, recitation, and
     discussion subsections that are supplementary in nature and are scheduled to meet separately from the lecture
     portion of the course. Undergraduate subsections are defined as any subsections of courses in which degree-
     seeking undergraduate students enrolled for credit. As above, exclude noncredit classes and individual instruction
    such as dissertation or thesis research, music instruction, or one-to-one readings. Each class subsection should be
     counted only once and should not be duplicated because of cross-listings.

should be counted only once and should not be duplicated because of cross‐listings.

I-3. Undergraduate Class Size
     In the table below, please use the following definitions to report information about the size of classes and
     class sections offered in the Fall 2021 term.
       •   Please include classes that have been moved online in response to the COVID-19 pandemic.

    Class Sections: A class section is an organized course offered for credit, identified by discipline and
    number, meeting at a stated time or times in a classroom or similar setting, and not a subsection such as a
     laboratory or discussion session. Undergraduate class sections are defined as any sections in which at
     least one degree-seeking undergraduate student is enrolled for credit. Exclude distance learning classes
    and noncredit classes and individual instruction such as dissertation or thesis research, music instruction, or
     one-to-one readings. Exclude students in independent study, co-operative programs, internships, foreign
    language taped tutor sessions, practicums, and all students in one-on-one classes. Each class section
     should be counted only once and should not be duplicated because of course catalog cross-listings.

    Class Subsections: A class subsection includes any subsection of a course, such as laboratory,
      recitation, and discussion subsections that are supplementary in nature and are scheduled to meet
     separately from the lecture portion of the course. Undergraduate subsections are defined as any
     subsections of courses in which degree-seeking undergraduate students enrolled for credit. As above,
     exclude noncredit classes and individual instruction such as dissertation or thesis research, music
      instruction, or one-to-one readings. Each class subsection should be counted only once and should not be
     duplicated because of cross-listings.

Class Sections: A class section is an organized course offered for credit, identified by discipline and
number, meeting at a stated time or times in a classroom or similar setting, and not a subsection such as a
laboratory or discussion session. Undergraduate class sections are defined as any sections in which at
least one degree-seeking undergraduate student is enrolled for credit. Exclude distance learning classes
and noncredit classes and individual instruction such as dissertation or thesis research, music instruction,
or one-to-one readings. Exclude students in independent study, co-operative programs, internships,
foreign language taped tutor sessions, practicums, and all students in one-on-one classes. Each class
section should be counted only once and should not be duplicated because of course catalog cross-
listings.

Class Subsections: A class subsection includes any subsection of a course, such as laboratory, recitation,
and discussion subsections that are supplementary in nature and are scheduled to meet separately from
the lecture portion of the course. Undergraduate subsections are defined as any subsections of courses in
which degree-seeking undergraduate students enrolled for credit. As above, exclude noncredit classes
and individual instruction such as dissertation or thesis research, music instruction, or one-to-one
readings. Each class subsection should be counted only once and should not be duplicated because of
cross-listings.
